title: Moon Dust Wore Through an Astronaut's Spacesuit Boots

scenes.text: Moon dust wore right through an astronaut's boots.
On Apollo 17, it chewed through the outer layer of the suit near the boots.
It had started reaching the layer underneath.
Under a microscope, it had even eroded the stainless-steel fibers.
On Earth, wind and water round off sand grains.
The Moon has neither, so the grains stay razor sharp.
The softest-looking powder on the Moon cuts through steel.
So yes: it wore through the boots.

description:
Moon dust wore right through an astronaut's boots.
On Apollo 17 it chewed through the outer layer of the suit, and microscopes showed it eroding the stainless-steel fibers.
Would you walk on the Moon knowing that?
first_comment: Bonus: Apollo astronauts said the dust smelled like gunpowder. What would Artemis crews do about it?
